analysis.title: Our 2027 outlook
key_insights: DB's expectation of a weaker dollar this year did not play out. The AI boom pushed US real rates higher, drew large equity inflows, renewed inflation pressure and produced a hawkish Fed.

The dollar could have been materially stronger given the oil shock and higher French political risk. Robust global growth, large US twin deficits, easing fixed income inflows and CNY strength limited appreciation pressure.

DB revises its 2027 dollar forecasts up. The path is a 'higher for longer' dollar, unusual against historical mean-reversion, with some strength into 1H27 and modest weakness in 2H27 that still leaves the dollar very elevated.

Support for the dollar comes from the US returning to the top of yield and growth rankings because of the AI boom, persistent equity inflows, the dollar's return as a high-yielder and a sharp compression in rate spreads against EM FX.

The main reason the forecast is not higher is the dollar's growing reliance on the AI capex boom. DB has high conviction that a sharper downgrade to capex expectations would lower US real rates and weaken equity inflows, removing the two key pillars of USD support.
A rotation from equities to bonds is unlikely to be enough to support the USD in that scenario, given evidence of rotation from US Treasuries to foreign bond markets.

Other negatives: hedge ratios on USD assets are biased upward as the diversification value of holding the USD unhedged falls, and lower energy prices could weaken the dollar. DB keeps a negative dollar bias further out, citing these risks and the large twin deficit.

The euro is likely to be weighed down by French political uncertainty and fairly aggressive ECB pricing. DB expects the balance of risks to improve through 2027 because French risk premium is already substantial, the election should reduce political fragmentation, and the macro backdrop is resilient.
Strong portfolio inflows are offsetting the weaker euro area current account. Fiscal spending and corporate health may raise the neutral rate from historic lows.

Asia FX has scope to outperform. AI-driven regional trade surpluses are recycled into US assets, which supports the 'chip dollar' cycle but adds circularity and exposure to an AI re-rating. DB sees that recycling weakening in 2027.
Japan: higher domestic yields, BoJ tightening and a policy push to mobilise savings at home could encourage capital repatriation, supporting USD/JPY moving into the 140s.
China: capital controls, geopolitical limits on US investment and greater exporter conversion of record trade surpluses should support continued low-vol CNH appreciation.
A shift of North Asian savings away from US assets would remove an increasingly important source of structural USD support.

EM: after a strong year there is less carry upside. Compressed rate spreads, heavy positioning and supply and fiscal risks make DB more cautious on CEEMEA and LatAm. Frontier markets and those with strong terms of trade and attractive valuations still offer selective upside.

macro_indicators.interpretation: DB sees USD/JPY moving into the 140s on capital repatriation from higher Japanese yields, BoJ tightening and a policy push to keep savings at home.

tension_points.bull_case: The US ranks first in yield and growth because of the AI boom, with persistent equity inflows and a high-yielder dollar against compressed EM rate spreads, which keeps the dollar elevated through 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The dollar depends increasingly on the AI capex boom. A more pronounced downgrade to capex expectations would push down US real rates and weaken equity inflows. Rotation to bonds is unlikely to offset it, and hedge ratios and lower energy prices add downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A more pronounced downgrade to AI capex expectations that lowers US real rates and weakens equity inflows.

theme_stances.evidence: the "AI dollar" is alive and well
